title: Republic of Djibouti
capsule: Djibouti occupies a strategic position at the southern entrance to the Red Sea, where the Gulf of Aden meets the Bab-el-Mandeb strait. It was colonized by France from the 1880s as French Somaliland (later the French Territory of the Afars and Issas) and gained full independence on 27 June 1977 under President Hassan Gouled Aptidon. The country's economy has been anchored by the Port of Djibouti and its role as the principal transit route for landlocked Ethiopia, while hosting the largest concentration of foreign military bases in Africa. A civil war between the Afar-dominated FRUD insurgency and the ruling Issa-dominated government, 1991–1994 and again 1999–2001, ended through negotiated agreements.
